14G.12 Health and healing come from obedience to the word and law of God.
15B.12 God will bless and deliver him that gives consideration to the poor.

precepts.text: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees: build up the spiritually weak brothers in every school, the inner circle and the trustworthy circle outside it. Say to them that are of a fearful heart, be strong, fear not; God hath not given us the spirit of fear. Behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence, a requital; he will come and save you. Isaiah 47:3 again: thy nakedness shall be uncovered by the word of God, and I will not meet thee as a man.
precepts.point: Some of you took the bag from the white man to sit up here in purple and report back. You have your house and car now, but the Most High has special destruction for sellouts and traitors, worse than the heathen's: weeping and gnashing of teeth, pain after death. Nowhere in the scriptures is there anything good for a traitor.
precepts.why:
David prays, “raise me up, that I may requite them”: raise me up the third day, so I can get vengeance on the traitor who ate of my bread. Isaiah tells the faithful to hold on for that vengeance: “Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.”

In every IUIC school some brothers may be weak and feeble, spiritually. Build them up. You have to build your inner circle up, loyal and faithful brothers who know the scriptures and fear God, and then have a circle outside of that of trustworthy, loyal men, so that when Jacob's trouble comes you don't all fall.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”. Brothers and sisters, be strong, because at times you might get afraid, but the Lord has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

Then: “behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” We must believe that our God will come with vengeance. A recompence is a requital, the same word as “that I may requite them” in the psalm: an appropriate return for wrongdoing.

Isaiah 47 shows that vengeance on Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”. All these fake Christians talking about America being a Christian society: their nakedness is uncovered by the word of God, and all their shameful deeds are revealed. “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” Christ is not coming back meeting them as a man. So strengthen the weak, fear not, and wait on the God who comes with recompence to save us.

precepts.text: The Lord has founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it. Zion is the Israelites, so the poor the Lord speaks of are the Israelites.
precepts.point: Blessed is he that considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble. This applies to the whole nation, because we are the poor.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” Zion is the Israelites, so the poor the Lord speaks of are the Israelites.

That is why this applies to the whole nation: we are the poor. The one who considers the poor, the Lord will preserve and keep alive, bless upon the earth, and not deliver “unto the will of his enemies.”

precepts.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven; the same thing, the poor are the Israelites.
precepts.point: Blessed is he that considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble. This applies to the whole nation, because we are the poor.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” The same thing: the poor are the Israelites, and the kingdom is theirs. Isaiah says the poor of his people trust in Zion, and Christ says the poor in spirit have the kingdom of heaven.

So “Blessed is he that considereth the poor” is about considering the Israelites, the whole nation. The Lord will deliver him in time of trouble and strengthen him “upon the bed of languishing”; and like David, he says “Lord, be merciful unto me: heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.”

precepts.text: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy; when I fall I shall arise, and when I sit in darkness the Lord shall be a light unto me. I will bear the indignation of the Lord because I have sinned, until he plead my cause; then she that is mine enemy shall see it and shame shall cover her, and she shall be trodden down as the mire of the streets. The Lord will fight on your behalf as long as you are doing what you must do.
precepts.point: Even his own familiar friend, in whom he trusted, who ate of his bread, has lifted up his heel against him. You have no clue who your real friends are until you fall.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“All that hate me whisper together against me: against me do they devise my hurt. An evil disease, say they, cleaveth fast unto him: and now that he lieth he shall rise up no more.” They rejoice in the affliction and disease David acquired through his transgressions. Micah answers that kind of enemy: “Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light unto me.”

“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me”. David owns his sin and bears the indignation, but the enemy who mocked it will see the outcome: “Then she that is mine enemy shall see it, and shame shall cover her which said unto me, Where is the Lord thy God? mine eyes shall behold her: now shall she be trodden down as the mire of the streets.” The Lord will fight on your behalf as long as you are doing what you must do.

This is a high level of hatred: “When shall he die, and his name perish?”, meaning when will this man be buried and just go. From other nations David is not surprised, but if you are in the truth and have this hatred toward your own people, that is wicked. When you fall in this truth, some spirits are built to mock and bring hurt to the spirit of the one who slipped, speaking vanity and flattering words to your face while the heart gathers iniquity, and slandering you abroad. Even his own familiar friend, in whom he trusted, who ate of his bread, lifted up his heel against him; you have no clue who your real friends are until you fall. But when I fall, I shall arise.

precepts.text: The Lord withdraws not his eyes from the righteous; if they be bound in cords of affliction, then he shows them their transgressions, opens their ear to discipline, and commands that they return from iniquity. If they obey they spend their days in prosperity; if not, they perish by the sword. Righteousness is not never sinning; it is being able to get back up, and if the Lord wants you, he will get you back right.
precepts.point: The Lord upholds David in his integrity and sets him before his face forever. The Lord kept him strong and moving in the right spirit.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“But thou, O Lord, be merciful unto me, and raise me up, that I may requite them.” Job shows how the Lord raises up a righteous man who has fallen: “He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted. And if they be bound in fetters, and be holden in cords of affliction; Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded. He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity. If they obey and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.” And if they do not obey, they perish by the sword.

Righteousness is not never sinning; it is being able to get back up. When the righteous are bound in cords of affliction, the Lord shows them their transgressions, opens their ear to discipline and commands them to return from iniquity. If the Lord wants you, he will get you back right.

That is how David knew the Lord favoured him: “mine enemy doth not triumph over me.” David went through much, including his own son trying to kill him and take the kingdom, but Absalom was not able to take the kingdom from him. The Lord upheld David in his integrity and set him before his face for ever; he kept him strong and moving in the right spirit, a king still on the throne.

moments.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me. This happened to David through Ahithophel, his own counsellor, who turned on him. And it is prophetic of somebody else.

The ones who leave are familiar friends. Some raised their children among us; imagine a child who grew from the womb to thirteen among the brethren, and the parents up and go over something that could have been resolved. That child loses everything he knows because of a wickedness his parents refused to confront.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: All that hate me whisper together against me; against me do they devise my hurt.

Zikanabiel taught twice on marriage in the last two weeks, and in one of those classes a sister told her husband, you had better find yourself another wife, because I am not doing anything a man tells me to do. Brothers, some of you are married to broken women, and a broken woman is unlovable. Video played of a young sister: I am angry, I am mad, I care more about you than you care about me, I am tired of feeling so much. She is broken. Now picture her walking in here.

Second video played, on trauma: the person who has been traumatized wants nothing more than love, but because it is so unfamiliar, when they get it they are suspicious of it, they reject it, they test it, and they punish the person trying to love them; but somebody who is neglectful and abusive feels familiar, and that one they love endlessly. Here you are, in this truth for a while, you get your life together, you tell the bishop, deacon and captain, I want to build a family; you prove her, you marry her, you try to love her the best you can, and she cannot accept it, because all her relationships have been chaos after chaos and you are trying to bring peace. She rejects the peace because she is not used to peace. I have seen this in Israel: why are you nice to me, why did you put me in a home, I am used to a broken home. That is a dangerous spirit, and brothers, that type of woman is the one who is going to betray you in these last days. Mark my words.

I know we jump from war to famine to relationships. Listen: they all come together. This is one event unfolding right in front of your eyes, like a chessboard, and as a man of God, a prophet, a leader, you cannot afford to miss anything; the minute you miss something, you are done.

Some of our people are the only people who do not understand honor. There was a woman upset that we clap when the bishop comes in; that same woman will clap for the president, clap for her boss, and clapped in the church, but now she is in Israel she has a problem. Just leave. We do not have time for that in these last days.

Mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me: Judas Iscariot, a traitor. Every IUIC sanctuary must have an inner circle of three to five loyal, faithful brothers who know the scriptures and fear God, not a circle of partiality of brothers who kiss your behind, or when Jacob's trouble comes you all fall. Traitors will be dealt with.

But thou, O Lord, be merciful unto me, and raise me up, the third day, that I may requite them: vengeance. By this I know that thou favourest me, because mine enemy doth not triumph over me. Judas and all who turned against Christ are back on this earth: Revelation 1:7, he cometh with clouds, his chariots they call UFOs, and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him. Matthew 16:28: there be some standing here which shall not taste of death till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom; those evil spirits do not taste death until he comes, and then they feel it.
Mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.
Men who want to be head in charge will be offered money to betray. Some will say, why teach the Bible, let's buy guns, and some will be wearing a wire.
Blessed is he that considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble. This applies to the whole nation, because we are the poor.
